Results.Title: At least 2 emergency access (break-glass) accounts
Results.Summary: 1 of 2 emergency access accounts (matching NamePatterns (no account listed in the Accounts parameter)) meet the requirements; at least 2 are needed.

Findings.Issues: no direct active Global Administrator assignment

Results.Description: Looks for emergency access accounts: the accounts listed in the Accounts parameter (UPNs or object ids) or, when the list is empty, users whose UPN or display name matches NamePatterns. An account is compliant when it follows the configuration requirements Microsoft documents: enabled, member, cloud-only (not synchronised), UPN on a `*.onmicrosoft.com` domain, and an **active** Global Administrator assignment made directly to the account (not only eligible in PIM, not through a group). Fails when fewer than **2** compliant accounts exist. Authentication methods, Conditional Access exclusions and sign-in alerting are part of the same guidance but are security controls outside the scope of ARGUS: verify them separately. Global exclusions are not applied.
Results.Rationale: Emergency access accounts prevent the organisation from being locked out of its tenant when federation, MFA or the usual administrators are unavailable. Microsoft recommends two or more, cloud-only, with a permanent active Global Administrator assignment.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Create two cloud-only accounts on the *.onmicrosoft.com domain, not tied to a person (for example breakglass01@contoso.onmicrosoft.com).
2. Assign Global Administrator directly and as active permanent (not eligible) in PIM.
3. Register phishing-resistant credentials (passkey/FIDO2 or certificate) different from the ones used by daily administrators, store them in separate safe locations, exclude the accounts from blocking Conditional Access policies and alert on every sign-in.
4. List the accounts in this check's Accounts parameter and test them at least every 90 days.

Results.Title: LinkedIn account connections disabled
Results.Summary: Manual verification required: the LinkedIn account connections setting cannot be read through Microsoft Graph. Check it in the Microsoft Entra admin center (Users > User settings); it should be No, or limited to a selected group.
Results.Description: The LinkedIn account connections setting (Microsoft Entra admin center > Users > User settings) lets users connect their work account to LinkedIn in Microsoft apps. It is enabled by default, except for organisations provisioned in Germany or France. Microsoft Graph has no documented API to read this setting, so ARGUS cannot evaluate it: the result is always Investigate and the setting must be checked manually. Expected value: **No** (or Selected group, if a business need was approved).
Results.Rationale: Once a user consents, Microsoft apps exchange profile and connection data between the work account and LinkedIn. Whether to allow it is an organisation decision about data sharing with a third-party service, and it should be explicit rather than left at the default.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center > Users > User settings.
2. Under LinkedIn account connections, check the current value.
3. Select No, or Selected group with a group of approved users, and save.
4. Record the decision; ARGUS will keep reporting this check as Investigate because the value cannot be read.

Results.Title: Global Administrator count outside 2 to 4
Results.Summary: 6 Global Administrators found (active assignments); the recommended range is 2 to 4. Eligible PIM assignments not evaluated: Entra ID P2 not detected.
Results.Description: Counts the distinct holders of the Global Administrator role: active assignments and, with Entra ID P2, eligible (PIM) assignments. Members of role-assignable groups that hold the role are counted individually. Fails when the count is below **2** or above **4**. Global exclusions are not applied: emergency-access accounts must be counted.
Results.Rationale: Too few Global Administrators risks losing control of the tenant; too many makes the most powerful role hard to govern. Keep two emergency-access accounts plus a small number of named administrators, and delegate the rest to least-privileged roles.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Keep two cloud-only emergency-access accounts with permanent Global Administrator assignments.
2. Move day-to-day administration to least-privileged roles (User, Exchange, SharePoint, Teams Administrator...).
3. With Entra ID P2, make the remaining Global Administrator assignments eligible in PIM instead of permanent.
Remediation.PowerShell:
# Sample only - review before running. Lists current Global Administrator assignments.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'RoleManagement.Read.Directory'
Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment -Filter "roleDefinitionId eq '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10'" -ExpandProperty principal

Results.Title: Client secrets with a lifetime above 24 months
Results.Summary: 5 client secrets have a lifetime longer than 24 months.
Results.Description: Valid client secrets whose lifetime (`endDateTime` minus `startDateTime`) exceeds **24** months. The admin center limits new secrets to 24 months, but secrets created through the API or before that limit can last much longer. Expired secrets are covered by ARG.APP.003.
Results.Rationale: Long-lived secrets are rarely rotated and outlive the people and documentation that explain them. Microsoft recommends less than 12 months, or certificates and managed identities instead.

Remediation.Steps:

2. Update the service that uses it, then delete the long-lived secret.

Results.Title: Unused licences per SKU
Results.Summary: 3 of 9 paid SKUs have more than 10% or more than 5 seats unused (81 unused seats in total).
Results.Description: Compares purchased seats (`prepaidUnits.enabled`) with assigned seats (`consumedUnits`) for every active, user-assignable SKU (`capabilityStatus` = Enabled, `appliesTo` = User). Results.Title: Shared mailboxes with a licence
Results.Summary: 2 of 14 shared mailboxes have a licence with no size, archive or hold that requires it (2 more are justified by size, archive or hold).
Results.Description: Shared mailboxes (Exchange Online) whose user object has licences assigned. Results.Title: Paid licences assigned directly to users
Results.Summary: 12 of 1,391 licensed users have paid licences assigned directly; 4 of them also receive the same licence from a group. 37 more have only free or trial licences assigned directly (not counted).
Results.Description: Users with at least one paid licence assigned directly (`licenseAssignmentStates` entry without `assignedByGroup`) instead of through group-based licensing. Free, viral and developer SKUs (the IgnoredSkus list), SKUs with **10,000** or more seats and trial SKUs (`isTrial` in `/directory/subscriptions`) are not counted: they are usually self-service sign-ups. AlsoFromGroup lists the direct licences the user also receives from a group, where the direct assignment is redundant.
Results.Rationale: Direct assignments are not driven by group membership: they are not removed when a person changes role or leaves, and they are hard to audit at scale. Group-based licensing keeps paid licences consistent with joiner/mover/leaver processes.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Create (or reuse) a security group per licence profile and assign the licences to the group.
2. Add the users to the group and wait for the group assignment to be active.
3. Remove the direct assignments, starting with the redundant ones listed in AlsoFromGroup.

# Sample only - review before running. Removes one directly assigned licence after the group assignment is active.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All'
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId '<ObjectId>' -AddLicenses @() -RemoveLicenses @('<SkuId>')

Results.Title: Users can register agent identity blueprints
Results.Summary: All users can register agent identity blueprints (allowedToCreateAgentIdentityBlueprints = true).
Results.Description: Reads `authorizationPolicy.defaultUserRolePermissions.allowedToCreateAgentIdentityBlueprints` ("Users can register agent identity blueprints" in Entra ID > Users > User settings) from the beta endpoint (`GET /beta/policies/authorizationPolicy`); v1.0 does not return it and Learn does not document it yet. The setting is independent of "Users can register applications" (ARG.ENT.010). Skipped when the tenant does not return the property yet.

Blueprints created by any user have no reviewed owner, purpose or permission scope, and every agent built on them inherits that gap. Restricting creation to administrators keeps agent identities inventoried and governed.

1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID > Users > User settings.
2. Set 'Users can register agent identity blueprints' to No and save.
3. Let administrators (or a dedicated role) create blueprints, and review the existing ones (GET /applications/microsoft.graph.agentIdentityBlueprint) for owner and purpose.

Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Policy.ReadWrite.Authorization'

Results.Title: Web search in Copilot is a deliberate choice
Results.Summary: Allow web search in Copilot is not configured: web search is available to users and its queries are outside the DPA and the EU Data Boundary.
Results.Description: Reads the tenant-level "Allow web search in Copilot" Cloud Policy setting (`GET /beta/copilot/admin/policySettings/microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch`, delegated sign-in only). When the policy is not configured, web search is available in Copilot and Copilot Chat (unless optional connected experiences are disabled): To review. The meaning of each configured value is not documented, so a configured value is To review unless it is listed in the `DisabledValues` parameter after you verified it in the Cloud Policy service. A group-scoped policy cannot be read by this API and is also To review.
Results.Rationale: With web search on, Copilot sends search queries derived from prompts (and sometimes from open documents) to Bing. Microsoft acts as data controller for those queries: the DPA, HIPAA and the EU Data Boundary do not apply to them. Whether that is acceptable is a privacy decision the organisation should take explicitly.

Remediation.Steps:
1. In the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center (config.office.com), open Customization > Policy Management.
2. Create or edit a policy with Allow web search in Copilot and choose Enabled, Disabled, or Disabled in Work mode only, according to the organisation's privacy decision.
3. Record the decision; after verifying the value ARGUS shows for the disabled option, add it to the DisabledValues parameter of ARG.COP.006 in the ARGUS configuration.

Results.Title: Guests without a sponsor
Results.Summary: 23 of 214 enabled guests have no sponsor.
Results.Description: Enabled guest users with no sponsor (`GET /users?$expand=sponsors`). Sponsors are the users or groups responsible for the guest's access and information; Microsoft Entra sets the inviter as sponsor for new invitations, so guests without one were usually invited before sponsors existed, lost a sponsor that left, or were invited by sharing a SharePoint file (a known case where no sponsor is set). Skipped when the account cannot read sponsors.
Results.Rationale: Without a sponsor nobody is accountable for the guest: access reviews have no reviewer, and the guest stays after the collaboration ends. A sponsor (a person or, better, a group) makes guest lifecycle decisions possible.

Remediation.Steps:
1. For each guest, find the team or project that collaborates with them (group memberships, the inviter in the audit log).
2. Add a sponsor in the Microsoft Entra admin center (Users > guest > Sponsors), preferably a group.
3. Remove guests that nobody wants to sponsor, and use sponsors as reviewers in guest access reviews.

Results.Title: Mailboxes with forwarding configured (inventory)
Results.Summary: 4 of 1,199 mailboxes forward mail (2 to external addresses); review each one.
Results.Description: Inventory of mailboxes with mailbox-level forwarding (`ForwardingSmtpAddress` or `ForwardingAddress` in `Get-EXOMailbox`). A forwarding SMTP address whose domain is not a verified domain of the tenant is marked External; `ForwardingAddress` points to a recipient in the directory (it can be a mail contact outside the organisation). Results.Rationale: Forwarding set years ago keeps copying mail to addresses nobody reviews, sometimes outside the organisation and after the owner left. Knowing where mail is forwarded, and why, is part of mailbox lifecycle governance; blocking automatic external forwarding is a security control outside the scope of ARGUS.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Review each forwarding with the mailbox owner or manager: target, reason, still needed.
2. Remove forwarding that is no longer needed (Exchange admin center > Mailboxes > mailbox > Mail flow settings > Email forwarding).
3. For leavers, replace forwarding with a shared mailbox or delegate access for a limited period.
Remediation.PowerShell:

Set-Mailbox -Identity '<mailbox>' -ForwardingSmtpAddress $null -ForwardingAddress $null -DeliverToMailboxAndForward $false

Results.Title: User mailboxes without a mailbox hold (informational)

Holds set mailbox by mailbox drift over time; knowing which mailboxes have one, and confirming that a retention policy covers the others, keeps the retention strategy consistent with legal requirements.

Remediation.Steps:
1. In the Microsoft Purview portal, check the retention policies that include Exchange mailboxes (Data lifecycle management > Policies > Retention policies).
2. If an organisation-wide policy covers all mailboxes, no mailbox hold is needed; document it.
3. Otherwise, apply a retention policy or Litigation Hold to the mailboxes that must be preserved.
